page.title: Formal Register and Nominalisation Basics
page.subtitle_html: Formal Register and Nominalisation Basics - B2 formal wording and basic noun-based alternatives.
page.subtitle_text: B2 formal wording and basic noun-based alternatives.

blocks.body: {"level":"B2","intro":"Formal Register and Nominalisation Basics: compact B2 anchors for formal verbs, noun phrases, and nominalisation.","rules":[{"label":"Formal verbs","text":"Use conduct, obtain, require, and indicate instead of more casual alternatives when needed.","example":"The team conducted a review."},{"label":"Nominalisation","text":"Turn actions into noun phrases for formal style.","example":"The improvement of the system is important."},{"label":"Register control","text":"Choose neutral or formal wording for reports, essays, and professional messages.","example":"Further information is required."}]}

blocks.heading: B2 focus
blocks.body: This compact page exists as the theory anchor for the English Sentence Builder B2 lesson package.

page.title: Nominalisation and Formal Register
page.subtitle_html: Nominalisation and Formal Register - C1 noun-based style, formal verbs, and controlled academic phrasing.
page.subtitle_text: C1 noun-based style, formal verbs, and controlled academic phrasing.

blocks.body: {"level":"C1","intro":"Nominalisation and Formal Register: compact anchors for turning actions into formal noun phrases.","rules":[{"label":"Action to noun","text":"Use a noun phrase when formal style needs distance or abstraction.","example":"The government made a decision to reduce expenditure."},{"label":"Formal verbs","text":"Choose verbs such as conduct, implement, indicate, and require in formal contexts.","example":"The committee conducted an evaluation of the proposal."},{"label":"Controlled register","text":"Avoid casual phrasing when an academic or professional tone is expected.","example":"Further analysis is required before publication."}]}

blocks.heading: C1 focus
blocks.body: This compact page exists as the theory anchor for the English Sentence Builder C1 nominalisation and formal register lesson package.

page.title: Register Tone and Paraphrase
page.subtitle_html: Register Tone and Paraphrase - C1 formal tone, neutral phrasing, and controlled sentence rewriting.
page.subtitle_text: C1 formal tone, neutral phrasing, and controlled sentence rewriting.

blocks.body: {"level":"C1","intro":"Register Tone and Paraphrase: compact anchors for shifting meaning into a controlled formal register.","rules":[{"label":"Formal tone","text":"Replace casual wording with precise neutral or formal alternatives.","example":"We would like to obtain further information about the results."},{"label":"Paraphrase","text":"Keep meaning stable while changing grammar, vocabulary, or information structure.","example":"The findings suggest that further analysis is required."},{"label":"Tone control","text":"Adjust certainty, politeness, and distance according to academic or professional context.","example":"It may be advisable to reconsider the proposal."}]}
